text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a sharp p99 token latency spike in ap-southeast-1 around 11:22 UTC. Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood/d/token-latency/token-latency?var-region=ap-southeast-1

eng-sre-bot: ALERT firing — TokenLatencyP99 > 800ms (5m) for region=ap-southeast-1. See: https://alertmanager.redwood/alerts/ALERT-2983

sophia: Looking — is this cold-starty or sustained? Any concurrent jump in tokens/sec or batch size?

alex: It was a sharp, sustained spike for ~8m. tokens/sec jumped at the same time from ~6k -> ~22k (5m rate). Query I used:
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
```
Also saw TTFT p95 increase aligned with p99.

liam: We rolled batching-config-v2 to ap-southeast canaries ~11:15 UTC (yesterday). Could be batch increase -> longer queueing for cold connections. deploy-bot: rollout/canary/batching-config-v2 -> started 2025-10-05T11:12:00Z.

natalie: Before we go deep on batching, can we check NAT/gateway SNAT exhaustion? Past incidents showed SNAT saturation causes huge tail latency (TLS handshake retries, RSTs).

alex: Checked quick Cloud metrics: SNAT concurrent connections for the subnet jumped to ~64k (limit ~65k) at 11:21. Also saw RST_rate spike on egress (snippet from tcpdump on nat-gw-2):
```
11:21:13.345 RST from 10.10.4.87:443 -> 10.0.1.12:53716
11:21:13.346 RST from 10.10.4.88:443 -> 10.0.1.15:53718
```
Connection churn + SNAT boundary looks suspicious.

liam: If SNAT is saturated new TLS connections stall/timeout -> worker threads block and batches grow -> token p99 climbs. Short term: increase NAT gateway count or attach extra Elastic IPs/ENIs.

sophia: For dashboards: add an annotated region-level panel that overlays deploy times + SNAT_conn_count + token_latency_p99. Also add a drilldown from p99 -> per-node token_latency_bucket and conntrack_count. We should tune the alert threshold: alert on p99>600ms for 5m in prod (instead of 800).

ops-alertbot: Alert suppressed by natalie (investigating) at 1765432160

alex: Mitigation applied: scaled NAT gateways + drained two nodes that had highest SNAT usage and restarted edge-proxies. p99 dropped from ~920ms -> ~240ms within ~2m after mitigation.

liam: Follow-ups: 1) autoscale egress endpoints / conntrack alarms 2) add connector to Grafana so the token p99 panel includes a direct link to conntrack and node-level latency buckets 3) add playbook steps for NAT saturation. I'll open infra ticket.

sophia: PromQL suggestions to add to dashboard drilldown:
```promql
sum(node_nat_conn_count) by (subnet)
sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[1m])) by (le, node)
```
Also add an annotation for deploys: query deploys via our events API and show them on the time-range.

natalie: Created INFRA-934: "ap-southeast-1 NAT connection saturation causing token p99 spikes" — includes remediation, timeline, and action items. CC: #eng-sre, #eng-runtime.

alex: :thumbsup: Marking this thread resolved for now. Will monitor panels and follow up on INFRA-934.
